solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Extra crop ruined at the farm (9)

indicators.note: what is ruined is wrecked and rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters of AT THE FARM rearranged

annotation.surface: A farmer's second harvest has failed.
annotation.walkthrough: "At the farm" reads as a setting for the ruin, but it is the raw material. An aftermath is literally a second growth of grass after mowing.
annotation.definitionFit: Aftermath originally meant a second mowing, the extra crop that grows after the first cut.

entries.clue: Nothing left? That’s OK (3,5)

blocks.note: if everything is on the right, nothing is left
an everyday phrase of reassurance, meaning fine

annotation.surface: Someone shrugs off having run out of everything.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left" looks like remaining, but it is the direction: if it is all right, none is left.
annotation.definitionFit: All right is a standard way of saying something is OK.

entries.clue: Made adjustments to first of Titian’s nude works (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the following word
the letters are worked over into a new order

annotation.surface: An art restorer has touched up one of Titian's nudes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Works" looks like paintings, a natural noun after Titian, but it is a verb telling you to rework NUDE.
annotation.definitionFit: To tune something is to make fine adjustments to it.

entries.clue: Tries again with a learner in practice session (9)

blocks.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it again
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A driving instructor has another go with a student.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tries" suggests attempts, but it is the legal sense: to rehear a case is to try it again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a practice run before a performance is the standard sense.

entries.clue: Incomplete expression of regret involving piece in annual publication (7)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
the outer word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: ALACK, an old cry of regret, without its last letter
a chess or draughts piece is a man

annotation.surface: A half-hearted apology about an article in a yearbook.
annotation.walkthrough: Alack is an archaic exclamation like alas. "Piece" means a game piece, not a written article.
annotation.definitionFit: An almanac is published once a year.

entries.clue: Hamlet’s first speech mainly for his friend (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of Hamlet
most of the word, so drop its last letter

annotation.surface: Hamlet's opening speech is mostly addressed to his friend.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface stays in Hamlet's world, so the answer hides in plain sight: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in the play.
annotation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play, Horatio is Hamlet's closest friend.

entries.clue: Examination that involves studying books (5)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a school exam; the setter means an inspection
the books are account books, a firm's financial records

annotation.surface: A student's exam requires reading textbooks.
annotation.walkthrough: The books are account books, not reading matter, and the examination is of them rather than of a pupil.
annotation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of an organisation's accounts, or books.

entries.clue: Like part of Greece that’s reached by final flight (5)

blocks.note: Attica is the region round Athens; its adjective describes things from there
a flight of stairs: the last one leads to the room under the roof

annotation.surface: A traveller lands in part of Greece on the last plane.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flight" suggests an aeroplane, but it is a flight of stairs; the top one leads to the attic.
annotation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica or Athens; an attic is the room under the roof, up the last stairs.

entries.clue: Send daily broadcast? Do that and be damned (6,3)

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer as an act that damns you rather than naming it

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

annotation.surface: A radio producer is told that a daily show is a damnable idea.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition works as a description: in Christian teaching, committing a deadly sin damns the soul.
annotation.definitionFit: The seven deadly sins are those said to lead to damnation.

entries.clue: Harden after short time in occupation (6)

indicators.note: the harden word comes after the time letter

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
enure is a variant spelling of inure, to harden

annotation.surface: Someone becomes toughened soon after starting a job.
annotation.walkthrough: ENURE is the less common spelling of inure.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding or occupation of a post or property.

entries.clue: Have some meal, uncharged? Never (5)

indicators.note: part of the following words

annotation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the idea of a free meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue plays on the saying "there's no such thing as a free lunch": a meal uncharged never happens.
annotation.definitionFit: The saying insists that a lunch at no charge never truly exists.

entries.clue: Book two for novelist (4,5)

blocks.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
twain is an old word for two

annotation.surface: Someone orders a second copy of a book for a writer.
annotation.walkthrough: "Book" is a book of the Bible, not a volume or a booking.
annotation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the American novelist who wrote Huckleberry Finn.

entries.clue: Shy and introspective, so expelled? Just the opposite (7)

blocks.note: breath expelled is drawn out; the opposite is drawn in, written as one word with the parts swapped

annotation.surface: A shy person is described, then corrected: not thrown out but the reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Expelled" suggests a school, but think of breath: breathed out is drawn out, so the opposite is drawn in.
annotation.definitionFit: Indrawn means withdrawn into oneself, reserved and introspective.

entries.clue: Equipment right for undertaker? (7)

definitions.note: undertaker here means one who undertakes or takes on a task, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: A funeral director needs the proper gear.
annotation.walkthrough: An undertaker usually buries the dead; here it is someone who undertakes, or tackles, a job.
annotation.definitionFit: One who tackles a job is one who undertakes it.

entries.clue: This rhapsodic introduction of Ravel’s transported musician (14)

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word
carried off, so the letters move to new places

annotation.surface: A performer is carried away by the opening of a Ravel rhapsody.
annotation.walkthrough: "Transported" looks like rapture at the music, but it moves the letters of THIS RHAPSODIC plus R.
annotation.definitionFit: A harpsichordist is a musician who plays the harpsichord.

entries.clue: Is a modern broadcast haphazardly set up? (9)

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a modern broadcast is put together carelessly.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: to randomise is to arrange by chance.
annotation.definitionFit: To randomise is to set things out in a haphazard, random order.

entries.clue: Spoke about one number overturning analysis of problem (9)

indicators.note: the spoke word goes round the others
in a down clue, turning over reverses the order

annotation.surface: Someone talks of a single figure upsetting a problem analysis.
annotation.walkthrough: "One number" looks like a single figure, but it is one plus a song. The whole assembly reads from the bottom up, so the answer opens with the verb backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of a problem by analysing its signs.

entries.clue: Supply key leads in careless fashion (8)

indicators.note: the key letter goes in front

blocks.note: supply as the adverb of supple, which is lithely

annotation.surface: Someone hands over keys and cables without care.
annotation.walkthrough: "Supply" is not provide but the adverb from supple, pronounced SUP-lee.
annotation.definitionFit: To act blithely is to act casually, without care or concern.

entries.clue: What ex-pat might view as something that divides us from Europe (7,7)

definitions.text: something that divides us from Europe

blocks.note: a Briton abroad might watch a TV channel in English

blocks.clueFragment: something that divides us from Europe
blocks.note: the sea strait between England and France

annotation.surface: A Briton abroad looks back across the water at home.
annotation.walkthrough: The first reading is a television channel in English; the second is the strait between England and France.
annotation.definitionFit: The English Channel is the sea separating Britain from mainland Europe.

entries.clue: Artist superior to Constable, reportedly (7)

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken aloud

blocks.note: a police sergeant ranks above a constable

annotation.surface: A critic claims some painter outranks John Constable.
annotation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter John Constable, which suits "artist", but it is the lowest police rank. John Singer Sargent was a portrait painter.
annotation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated American portrait artist.

entries.clue: Topical reforms in American political scene (7)

indicators.note: forms again, in a new order

annotation.surface: Current reforms are under way in Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: "Reforms" fits politics so well it reads as a noun, but it is the verb that rearranges TOPICAL.
annotation.definitionFit: The Capitol in Washington is where the US Congress meets.

entries.clue: The writer ultimately diminished great singer as tragic high-flier (6)

indicators.note: cut at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
CARUSO, the great tenor, without his last letter

annotation.surface: A writer ends up belittling a famous singer as a doomed star.
annotation.walkthrough: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian tenor. Icarus flew too near the sun and fell.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew so high that his wax wings melted.

entries.clue: Trumpet introducing bit of music – it makes a forceful entry (7)

indicators.note: the trumpet word comes first, bringing in the next

blocks.note: to trumpet a success is to crow about it
a bar is a short section of music

annotation.surface: A fanfare announces a dramatic arrival.
annotation.walkthrough: "Trumpet" looks like the instrument beside the music, but it is the verb meaning to boast.
annotation.definitionFit: A crowbar is used to force doors and windows open.

entries.clue: Hairstyle worn by sailor and his colleague (5)

indicators.note: the hairstyle is put on around the sailor

annotation.surface: A sailor and a shipmate both sport the same hairdo.
annotation.walkthrough: "His colleague" points back to the sailor: a bosun is a ship's officer, a fellow seaman.
annotation.definitionFit: The bosun, or boatswain, works alongside the ordinary sailors on a ship.

entries.clue: Piece of jewellery author and poet shortened (7)

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A writer and a poet cut down a necklace.
annotation.walkthrough: "Author" is the verb, to write, which is to pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: this jewellery hangs, and its name comes from the Latin for hanging.

entries.clue: Friend from Europe with another on journey (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: another friend from Europe: ami is French for friend

annotation.surface: A European pal travels with a companion.
annotation.walkthrough: "Another" leans on the definition: another friend from Europe is the French AMI. Amigo is Spanish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain translation: the word is Spanish, and Spain is in Europe.

entries.clue: Once more check and control cult holding power (9)

indicators.note: the cult word holds the power letter inside

annotation.surface: An inspector checks again and curbs a sect's influence.
annotation.walkthrough: "Check" and "control" sit side by side as if meaning the same, but only the first is part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means again, so this is an inspection repeated.

entries.clue: Sound of delightful musical sequence (5)

indicators.note: the answer sounds like the word

annotation.surface: Someone admires a lovely piece of music.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as praise for music, which neatly hides that "sound of" is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A suite is a set of musical movements played in sequence.

entries.clue: Republican welcomed by gun firm (5)

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so the gun takes in the Republican

blocks.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

annotation.surface: A gun company takes in a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: "Firm" looks like a company to go with the gun, but it is the adjective meaning strict.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the strict sense, as of a parent who will not give way.

entries.clue: Politician of considerable stature swallowing second dubious account (4,5)

indicators.note: the politician phrase takes the letter inside

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A prominent politician falls for a questionable tale.
annotation.walkthrough: "Of considerable stature" suggests importance, but it is literal height. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A tall story is an account too far-fetched to believe.
